name: GET /api/leadflow/consent/suppressions - the effective state per channel
description:
Answers 'may we contact this person, and on which channels' for one subject, as five per-channel verdicts plus a single any_suppressed flag.

DERIVED, NOT STORED (AC4). There is no 'currently suppressed' column to read: the ledger is append-only and this endpoint computes the current state from it, using the same rule the channel-decision composer applies. That is the point - a screen that showed one answer while the composer acted on another would be worse than showing nothing, and a stored flag drifts from the signal log the moment either is written without the other.

MOST-RESTRICTIVE WINS, AND THE TIE-BREAK IS THE POINT. Two sources can disagree: a provider webhook says suppressed, a staff member has just pressed release, a reconciliation has inserted a stop dated yesterday. The rule is implemented as the ORDER BY rather than a comparison in application code - `signal = 'release'` sorts LAST within a timestamp, so a stop and a release recorded in the same instant resolve to SUPPRESSED. That is the only safe tie-break: holding a message that could have gone is an inconvenience, and sending one that should have been held is a breach.

PER-CHANNEL, SO A RELEASE CAN BE NARROW. Verified live: a subject suppressed on all five channels by one sms_stop, then released on email alone, reads email:false and sms/call/social/push:true - and the channel-decision composer agrees, answering review on email and deny on sms for the same subject in the same second.

EACH CHANNEL CARRIES THE SIGNAL AND THE INSTANT, not just a boolean. 'Suppressed since when, and because of what' is what an operator needs to answer a subject asking why they stopped hearing from us, and a bare true cannot answer either half.

EDGE CASES: subject_ref is required - there is no list-everything form, because the register of everybody who ever opted out is a disclosure in its own right rather than a browse surface. A subject with no signals at all reads as five channels of suppressed:false with null signal and null since, rather than 404: never having been suppressed is a real and useful answer, not a missing record.

Governed rather than merely authenticated: reading who opted out is itself a disclosure, so who looked belongs in the record. requiresRole:["privacy_officer"] and NO testCase pins an Authorization header (MUST-71). QA: depends on register, login and a recorded stop signal.

testCases.name: Reports every channel, with the signal and the instant behind each
A subject who never opted out is answered, not 404'd
NEGATIVE: no subject_ref, so there is nobody to report on
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all

errorCases.when: subject_ref is absent or blank. There is deliberately no list-everything form: the register of everybody who ever opted out is a disclosure rather than a browse surface.

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the header is absent or not Bearer

errorCases.message: No policy grants this action to the caller's roles.
errorCases.when: the caller does not hold consent.purpose_manage
errorCases._whyNotReproducible: MUST-64/MUST-71: it needs a token from a DIFFERENT role, and this definition declares requiresRole so the runner pre-fetches the privacy_officer identity. Pinning a second role's Authorization header alongside requiresRole is what MUST-71 forbids.
